characters.description: The main character of the series, a seventeen-year-old girl struggling with drug addiction and her identity. She often latches onto other people as a way to feel complete. Abusive Offspring: In the depths of her addiction, she verbally abuses Leslie, lies to her, violently assaults her, and kicks down a door. Addiction Displacement: Gets clean just to become addicted to Jules, who she compares to fentanyl at one point. Affectionate Nickname: Cassie likes to call her Rue-Rue. Aimlessly Seeking Happiness: In the pilot, Rue explains that doing drugs makes her feel better and that she's been "chasing" that feeling for as long as she can remember. But of course, the high is only temporary.

characters.name: Rue Bennett
characters.description: The main character of the series, a seventeen-year-old girl struggling with drug addiction and her identity. She often latches onto other people as a way to feel complete. Abusive Offspring: In the depths of her addiction, she verbally abuses Leslie, lies to her, violently assaults her, and kicks down a door. Addiction Displacement: Gets clean just to become addicted to Jules, who she compares to fentanyl at one point. Addled Addict: At her worst, Rue is unstable due to her addiction. In Season 2, she outright snaps from it, attacking and screaming at everyone around her. Aesop Amnesia: Despite the dangerous situations she keeps getting into, Rue rarely learns anything, particularly regarding consequences or just the severity of the moment. After being dragged into the drug deal with the intimidating Laurie and her violent underlings in the opening of Season 2, Rue clearly hasn't absorbed anything from the experience except for admiring Laurie being a female drug dealer, Fez having to berate her for treating the whole event like it was fun.

characters.name: Jules Vaughn
characters.description: A pretty and fashionable trans girl who befriends Rue at a party. She tries to help other people with their problems, but often ends up wearing herself thin. Age-Gap Romance: She often engages in sexual activities with older men she meets on Grindr. All Girls Want Bad Boys: DarklyPlayed With. Jules falls hard in love for thekind, good hearted guy "Tyler" during their time texting together, with the two sharing a great deal of intimacy together, but is horrified when she finds out he wasNateall along, who uses it all as blackmailing material against her. Despite this, she can't seem to let go of her feelings towards "Tyler", having great internal conflict trying to reconcile the seeming two vastly differing sides of Nate's personality. Making matters even more confusing, Nate ends up confirming that everything they had shared had been real on his part, not merely an act, and that he regrets what he did to her. Despite it all, even years later she seems to still carry fond feelings for Nate, and is entirely at ease with him. The Alcoholic: Jules seems to have a complicated relationship with alcohol. Special mention go to her drinking heavily at the Halloween partyto numb her sorrows, and enjoying a Gatorade and Everclear mix just a little too much. In season 3, she drinks heavily and is rarely seen without a cigarette in hand. Badass Adorable: Despite being a sweet and friendly girl, her first conversation withJerk JockNate has herpointing a knife at himafter he threatens her.

characters.name: Maddy Perez
characters.description: Alcoholic Parent: Her father is "in between jobs", but often spends his days drunk in front of the TV. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She's in a relationship with the aggressive, violent Nate, though she doesn't always like his crueler tendencies. But, it got deconstructed later on. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: At times, although it's implied mostly to come from theStepford Smilernecessity of staying with Nate, a domestic abuser. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Naz remarks Maddy must truly love Cassie to go through so much trouble to help her when she's held hostage. In spite of everything, Maddy does indeed seem to really care for Cassie. Beauty Breeds Laziness: Maddy's life plan was to use her good looks to land a rich boyfriend and become a kept woman. Unfortunately for her, she's ended up in a toxic relationship with Nate Jacobs, the abusive scion of a wealthy, dysfunctional family, and he takes advantage of her lack of self-preservation instincts in order to control her. However, she grows out of this little by little as she starts making her own living.

characters.name: Cassie Howard
characters.description: All for Nothing: After destroying her friendships, walking out on her family, and allowing Nate to completely control her life, Nate ends up dumping her and kicking her out of his house after Lexi's play mocks him.Her situation in Season 3 doesn’t get any better, as her marriage to Nate quickly unravels because of how financially strapped he becomes. And despite the opportunity Maddy gives her to make a name for herself on herOnlyFansaccount, she also ends up biting off more than she can chew when she signs Maddy’s legal contract without realizing that it conflicts with a recent role she earned on “LA Nights”, a series project (albeit by accidental improvisation) created by the studio her sister is working for, and is required to give up herOnlyFansaccount. As a result, once the studio and platform distributing network finds out this fact, they’re quick to drop her from the role. It also ties into her relationship with Nate, who has been frequently hounded by Naz and his loan sharks despite her wiring some of her earnings to Nate; because her source of income is gone, this gets her kidnapped and nearly killed. Maddy making a deal with Alamo to save her and her husband also ends up not panning out, because by the time they get to Nate, he’s already dead himself from a rattlesnake attack. Her situation in Season 3 doesn’t get any better, as her marriage to Nate quickly unravels because of how financially strapped he becomes. characters.name: Lexi Howard
characters.description: A shy, responsibleBrainy Brunettewho often ends up picking up the slack when it comes to her friends' reckless endeavors. Doesn't speak up much about her problems much, but it's clear that she's struggling nonetheless. Allegedly Dateless: Lexi is supposed to be a more isolated, down to earth character who's unlucky in love and regarded as less pretty than Cassie. She has been asked out before and almost immediately in Season 2 forms a very close bond with Fez. All Girls Want Bad Boys: She falls for drug dealer Fezco. All Take and No Give: Is the “Giver” in this type of dynamic with both Rue and, to a lesser extent, Cassie. Ambiguously Bi: Lexi lacks a male love interest in the first season, unlike many of the characters in the show. Her mom makes mention of her “girlfriends” several times, and it is implied that she may have feelings for Rue, with her gazing longingly at her throughout the series, and her unreadable expression when Gia tells her she thinks Rue loves Jules. Plus there is a scene late in the season where Lexi states that she isn't interested in the guys who are enamored with her, and while Cassie tells her that she will eventually find a guy, she looks increasingly unsure. This is subverted to a degree come the second season when she develops a crush on Fez, indicating that at the very least she is not a lesbian.

characters.name: Nate Jacobs
characters.description: Maddy'saggressive and manipulative jockboyfriend, with severe psychological issues regarding his sexuality and masculinity. Agony of the Feet: In Season 3, Naz, a Loan Shark, cuts Nate’s toe off for failing to pay him back. Ain't Too Proud to Beg: At a city council meeting, he literally begs on hands and knees to be able to resume construction so he can make money to pay Naz back. The council refuses, much to his devastation. Ambiguously Bi: He's in a relationship with Maddy, whom he's obsessed over and subjects to domestic abuse. At the same time, he has also seems to be following in his dad's footsteps by using Grindr, a gay dating app, but it later turns out he'd only used it to find Jules so that he could blackmail her into leaving his father alone. However, he does confess to Maddy to being confused, adding ambiguity to the situation. Plus there's the matter of him having numerous dick pics on his phone that aren't his. And it is heavily implied he really did fall in love with Jules accidentally in the process of blackmailing her, based on his later actions against his father, retrieving her tape and his confession to her that what they shared had been genuine on his part. Antagonistic Offspring: Towards his father Cal, whom he resents to the point of nearly assaulting him in the Season 1 finale. In Rue's narration, she also mentions that Nate doesn't like his mother because he considers her "weak."

characters.name: Leslie Bennett
characters.description: Rue and Gia's strong and empathetic mother, who struggles to keep her two daughters in check. It appears as if she's still mourning the loss of Rue's dad, even though she does gain a string of boyfriends. Commuting on a Bus: As of Season 3, Leslie remains in East Highland but has cut off all contact with Rue due to her inability to handle her daughter's drug use that had negative effect on Gia. In 3x06, Leslie contacts Rue to check on her and only makes a brief appearance as the call ends. Demoted to Extra: Due to theTime Skip, Leslie is understandably reduced to this in season 3, as Rue is no longer living in East Highland nor her house roof just as she had promised. She appears in the sixth episode, but has only a single line while contacting Rue. Glamorous Single Mother:Subverted. It's made abundantly clear that Leslie is fearful for Rue's health while also appearing frightened at the possibility of her daughter Gia going down the same route. Has a Type: Based on her late husband and her boyfriend Rick, she likes long-nosed, somewhat dorky whiteNice Guytypes.

characters.name: Cal Jacobs
characters.description: Affably Evil: He seems to have cultivated an image as a traditionalFamily Manin the town. In reality, he consistently and often cheats on his wife, mainly withmuchyounger partners such as the seventeen-year-old Jules. He can also be a huge bully, as seen in Season 2 when he aggressively pressures Cassie into revealing who assaulted Nate (in front of Lexi and their mother no less), but he never loses his affability, even seeming genuinely disturbed by finding out that Jules is underage. Ain't Too Proud to Beg:When Jules reveals herself to him at the chili cookoff, Cal finds her when she's alone and says he knows she can destroy him by revealing they had sex. He outright begs her not to, unaware Jules has no intention of doing so.In the Season 2 finale, Nate approaches him and lets him know about the trauma he suffers as a result of having seen his videos at a young age. He produces a flash drive containing all of the videos, and Cal hears the approaching sirens of police, which were tipped off by him ahead of time. Cal begs Nate not to send him away, in the most vulnerable and fearful state we've ever seen him in thus far, but Nate simply says that he doesn't believe he will ever change, and the police arrive and arrest him shortly after. When Jules reveals herself to him at the chili cookoff, Cal finds her when she's alone and says he knows she can destroy him by revealing they had sex. He outright begs her not to, unaware Jules has no intention of doing so. characters.name: Elliot
characters.description: A new student at East Highland who becomes friends with Rue and infatuated with Jules. Ambiguously Bi: When asked by Jules about his sexuality, he responds he is "kinda" straight and "kinda" gay. He says he has fucked 3 women, but they were bad, and jokes of having sex with 43 men. Distaff Counterpart: To Rue. He's aFunctional Addictwith a similar style of dress (right down to the black Converse) and feelings for Jules, but maintains much healthier relationships and has lessKick the Dogmoments, showing much more support for his friends. Hypocrite: Is one for telling Leslie about Rue's relapse despite being a major purveyor of drugs for Rue. Karma Houdini: Starts an affair with Jules, rats out Rue’s drug use, and generally drives a huge wedge between them all season—and doesn’t really face any comeuppance for it.

characters.name: Fezco
characters.description: A sweet, non-threatening drug dealer and one of Rue's close friends. Fezco has a mild demeanor, but can easily resort to violence when provoked. Affably Evil: Fez is a drug dealer who will sell to children — but he's also one of the nicest characters. Back for the Finale: ThoughAngus Clouddied before production on Season 3 started, the series uses aDeleted Scenebetween Rue and Fez in the series finale as Rue realizes she's dying. Beware the Nice Ones:He threatens to kill Nate when he goes near Rue, and later beats a doctor into unconsciousness when robbing the man's home (though, to be fair, he didn't expect the man or his son to be home at that time).In the premiere episode of Season 2, Fez has had it with Nate and violently assaults him at a party, brutally beating him into unconsciousness. He threatens to kill Nate when he goes near Rue, and later beats a doctor into unconsciousness when robbing the man's home (though, to be fair, he didn't expect the man or his son to be home at that time).

characters.name: Kat Hernandez
characters.description: A withdrawn, sensibleBig Beautiful Womanwho slowly starts gaining confidence and popularity as she gains more traction with boys. Amicable Exes: Despite how their break-up went, she and Ethan seemingly become this at the end of Season 2 as Kat is seen enjoying his performance during Lexi's play and cheers for him. Artists Are Attractive: A guy interested in her compliments her artistic choice of make-up. Beautiful All Along: A strange version. Kat discovers that she's genuinely been attractive her whole life, and that her insecurity about her weight prevented her from seeing it. Once she gets confident, she hasmultiplemen wanting her attention. Be a Whore to Get Your Man: Shereallywants to lose her virginity in order to appear as less of a "prude", at least among the male population of the school.

characters.name: Ethan Daley
characters.description: Disappointed in You: WhenKattries to manipulate himto break up with her, he sees through the ploy and walks away. He doesn't say it outright, but it's clear that he's very upset and irritated moreso than angry. Dogged Nice Guy: He's consistently nice towards Kat, who initially rebuffs him (granted she thought he was flirting with another girl). However, this doesn't stop him from still being kind to her and pursuing her. Drama Club: He was involved in Lexi’s Play. Hidden Depths: Ethan wasn’t given much development outside of Kat until Lexi’s play showed him to be a versatile and talented actor, playing a multitude of roles - particularly the parodies of Nate and Cassie's and Lexi's mom - and receiving adoring reactions from the crowd. Jizzed in My Pants: Ethan does this while giving Kat oral sex, to his embarrassment.

characters.name: Ashtray
characters.description: A scarily childlike drug dealer who doesn't appear to be older than around thirteen. He's Fezco's younger brother, and the pair appear to be relatively close. Character Death: Killed in the final episode of Season 2. Dirty Kid: He's a scrawny-looking adolescent with tattoos and asurprisingamount of experience with illicit drugs. The Dragon: A non-villainous example. He’s Fezco's right-hand man and seems to handle the day-to-day and distribution side of their business. While Fez is slow to respond to business complications, Ashtray usually takes decisive action to solve problems. The two biggest plot events in their arc, the killings of Mouse and Custer, occur by his hand. Everyone Has Standards:Invoked, he says he draws the line at human trafficking.

characters.name: Gia Bennett
characters.description: Rue's sweet younger sister, who ends updabbling in drugsby the end of Season 1. One of the few people Rue genuinely cares about. Annoying Younger Sibling:Subverted. Gia seems close to her older sister. The Baby of the Bunch: She's one of the youngest characters and an absolute sweetheart. Break the Cutie: She's absolutely adorable, which makes it even more heart-wrenching when she startsusing drugs.Lampshadedby Ali, who seems to partially blame Rue for what her sister has had to deal with. Broken Bird: Gia spends most of Season 2 crying for understandable reasons, as she's being gaslit by her sister's drug use and trying to defend her.

characters.name: ChristopherMcKay
characters.description: McKayis Cassie's boyfriend and a gifted football player. He has trouble adjusting to college, citing a worry of not being "the best of the best". Child Hater:Downplayed. He proclaims that "children are fucking scary" uponfinding out that Cassie's pregnantand eventuallypushes her to get an abortion, as he doesn't feel ready to be a dad. Demoted to Extra:McKayis a fairly prominent character in the first season, but afterhe breaks it off with Cassie for good and brings an injured Nate to the hospitalhe is not seen for the rest of Season 2. Fiendish Fraternity: AfterMcKay's fraternity brothers see Cassie at a party, they pinMcKaydown and shout sexual things at him. He's deeply affected by the experience. Freudian Excuse: His dad pushed him to be the best in football and to suppress his emotions, though this pressure has led toMcKayhavingJerkasstendencies.

characters.name: Ali Muhammad
characters.description: Abusive Parents: He had an abusive father during his childhood and vowed not to be like that to his daughters, especially after he had struck their mother in an argument during his days as an addict. As the Good Book Says...: When Rue is easily forgiven by Ali and she asks him why, he answer with a poignant quote fromThe Qur'an."The Hour is certain to come, so we must forgive graciously." The Atoner: It's implied that hisTough Loveaffection for Rue stems from a deep need to make amends with the family he's harmed in the past. Badass in a Nice Suit: He shows up for Alamo in his military uniform. Brutal Honesty: Ali does not believe in mincing his words. When Rue's mother asks if Rue can get clean, he says very clearly he doesn't know, while Rue is right there.

characters.name: Suze Howard
characters.description: Actually Pretty Funny: Unlike other characters who are either deeply uncomfortable or furious, she is delighted by the version of her Lexi writes in her play and by Ethan's portrayal of her. Alcoholic Parent: There isn't a scene with Suze where sheisn'tdrunk or drinking. Brutal Honesty: Suze doesn't have much of a filter, least of all towards her daughters. Clingy Jealous Girl: In flashbacks, she's shown getting extremely jealous whenever someone flirts with her handsome husband, but then hypocritically has an affair of her own. Deadpan Snarker: Suze has a witty remark for every occasion.Suze: Hey, creepy. The whole point of Halloween is to look attractive.Lexi: No, it's not.Suze: Oh, really? You do me a favor and you count how many girlfriends of yours are dressed up like 50-year-old men. Report back to me.

characters.name: Daniel Dimarco
characters.description: Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: After going steady for a long time as kids, Daniel breaks up with Kat for her weight gain. As a young adult, he admits to only being interested in Cassie because he wanted to have sex with her. He ends uphaving sex with Kat, and despite her valuing their brief previous relationship, he says he already forgot about that and leaves Kat with a hurt look on her face. But for Me, It Was Tuesday: After hooking up with Kat, she mentions them dating when they were younger, something he doesn't even remember. Meanwhile, for Kat, it was apretty big deal, and a focal point in her body image issues. Break Them by Talking: What heenjoysdoing the most. For the Evulz: He degrades almost every woman he dates, namely Kat and Cassie and ruins their self-esteem just for his own amusement. Hate Sink: Daniel is nothing but aStraw Misogynistwho degrades and uses both Cassie and Kat and spitefully hurts them when he gets bored of them.

characters.name: Tyler Clarkson
characters.description: Frame-Up:In order to not be held accountable for cheating on Nate publicly, Maddy claims she was blacked out, painting Tyler as having raped her while she was too drunk to consent. While he did have sex with an underage girl, he assumed she was in college.Using that information,Nate blackmails Tyler into a falsely admit to be the one to attack Maddy, so the blame is out of him. In order to not be held accountable for cheating on Nate publicly, Maddy claims she was blacked out, painting Tyler as having raped her while she was too drunk to consent. While he did have sex with an underage girl, he assumed she was in college. Using that information,Nate blackmails Tyler into a falsely admit to be the one to attack Maddy, so the blame is out of him. Butt-Monkey: Seriously, this guycannotcatch a break and the majority of his screentime is spent getting beaten up or humiliated.

characters.name: TroyMcKayand RoyMcKay
characters.description: Always Identical Twins: They look alike each other. Annoying Younger Sibling: They have shades of this towards Chris in the first episode. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: They haven’t been mentioned nor have been appeared in season 2. The Stoner: They enjoy weed and are often seen stoned. Theme Twin Naming: Their names sound similar to their brother's.

characters.name: Luke Kasten
characters.description: Jaded Washout: He used to be a BMOC and is a famousSex Godbut now he is a mediocre guy working in retail and is fucking a teenage dominatrix who concludes he is pathetic. Urban Legend Love Life: He's famous at the group's school because of this even years after he graduated.

characters.name: David Vaughn
characters.description: Jules's dad. He works from home and seems to structure his whole life around his daughter. Extreme Doormat: He seems to have structured his whole life around keeping Jules happy, and doesn't seem to lay down any kind of rules. I Need a Freaking Drink: In the first-season finale, as Jules and Rue head out to the dance, he jokes that he and Leslie plan to get plastered. Open-Minded Parent: He loves his transgender daughter, and doesn't bat an eye at her bringing her black girlfriend home to sleep over all the time. Put on a Bus: He does not appear in Season 3, and is only mentioned once when Jules talks to him on the phone about art school.

characters.name: Marsha Jacobs
characters.description: Nate's mother and Cal's wife. The Beard:Downplayed. Cal is bisexual and was shown to be genuinely in love and attracted to her as a teenager; however, it's clear he'd much rather had ended up with a man (specifically Derek, his male best friend from high school) and never truly wanted to marry her. This is as evident in his adulterous hookups, none of whom seem to be cisgender women. But for Me, It Was Tuesday: The first time she met Jules was at the carnival when she passed by their chili stand. However, in Season 3, when Cal tells her who she is at Nate and Cassie's wedding (a friend of Nate's, as he refers), Marsha claims that she doesn't remember her. Everyone Has Standards:It’s downplayed, but evenMarshafelt as if Nate shouldn't choke Maddy, despite admitting that she wanted to do so herself. Female Misogynist: Type 6, in that she looks down onMaddyfor being promiscuous and not good enough for Nate, but has no issues with Caucasian girls such asNatalie(who he took to winter ball) andCassiegoing out with him.

characters.name: Laurie
characters.description: A drug dealer to whom Rue comes to owe a lot of money. The Aggressive Drug Dealer:Reconstructed. Laurie doesn't seem aggressive, and in fact, she says that she's never gotten angry in her life.However, it should not be mistaken that Laurie is also an extremely dangerous person — it's just that she likes to be calm about it. Affably Evil: Laurie is perhapsthemost frightening character in the whole series, when it becomes clear that she is prepared to prostitute Rue and get her addicted tootherdrugs, but she is nothing but polite and even genuinely understanding of Rue's plight. She's still evil, though. Ambiguous Situation: It's heavily implied, but never explicitly stated, that Laurie knew all along that Rue would never be able to pay back the money she owed her for the drugs and that she always intended to traffic her since their first meeting. Better to Die than Be Killed: She commits suicide rather than be taken by the DEA.

characters.name: Faye
characters.description: Custer’s girlfriend who begins living with Fezco and Ashtray in Season 2. Dumb Blonde: Basically her entire personality; probably even denser than Cassie. Heel–Face Turn:Faye betrays Custer to warn Fezco shortly before the raid. Hidden Depths: It’s implied that her ditziness stems from her drug addiction as she proves to be useful and competent when she’s sober and when she’s around Fez and Ash. Hypocritical Humor: In "Trying to Get to Heaven Before They Close the Door", Faye calls Rue a "fucking junkie ass bitch" while lighting up a heroin spoon.

characters.name: Bruce
characters.description: A drug dealer who works for Laurie. Affectionate Nickname: Laurie calls him “Brucey.” The Aggressive Drug Dealer: The more outwardly aggressive of him and Laurie, and the one who puts hands on Fez, Rue, Ashtray, and Faye when Laurie suspects they're hiding wires during the drug trade while she stands by. Even Evil Has Loved Ones: A hardened and remorseless drug dealer and murderer who most likely also engages in human trafficking, as Laurie does. Nevertheless, he appears to genuinely care about Laurie. Even Evil Has Standards:When he has Rue and the others strip down to be checked for wires, he forces Ashtray into the closet because he is a child. Rue, who is also underage, does not receive this grace, however.In Season 3, when Rue almost dies of ingesting drug balloons, his first instinct is to carry her back to Laurie's place for recovery.

characters.name: Faye Valentine
characters.description: Custer’s girlfriend who begins living with Fezco and Ashtray in Season 2. Dumb Blonde: Basically her entire personality; probably even denser than Cassie. Heel–Face Turn: Faye betrays Custer to warn Fezco shortly before the raid. Hidden Depths: It’s implied that her ditziness stems from her drug addiction as she proves to be useful and competent when she’s sober and when she’s around Fez and Ash. Hypocritical Humor: In "Trying to Get to Heaven Before They Close the Door", Faye calls Rue a "fucking junkie ass bitch" while lighting up a heroin spoon.

characters.name: Alamo Brown
characters.description: A rival drug kingpin to Laurie. Always a Bigger Fish: He dispatches Naz on Maddy's request for Cassie's sake. Maddy quickly realizes this was not as beneficial as she'd hoped as he takes the chance to state that now they owe him a million dollars and twenty of all future earnings. And Now You Must Marry Me: He's not satisfied with just money from Maddy. He intends to create a new American dream for himself by forcing her into marriage as a devoted housewife raising children for him. And There Was Much Rejoicing: Nobody is sad to see him go. For Ali, it's avenging Rue. Bishop is coldly satisfied and seems poised to take over. The girls are free from his tyranny and Maddy cannot restrain her visible joy at his death. Bad People Abuse Animals: One sign of Alamo being nasty is he's callous about animals, coldly gunning down a pig released back into his club and ordering Bishop to poison Laurie's cockatoo Paladin.

characters.name: ChrisMcKay
characters.description: McKayis Cassie's boyfriend and a gifted football player. He has trouble adjusting to college, citing a worry of not being "the best of the best". Child Hater:Downplayed. He proclaims that "children are fucking scary" upon finding out that Cassie's pregnant and eventually pushes her to get an abortion, as he doesn't feel ready to be a dad. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: As of Season 3,McKayhas been completely forgotten by the rest of the characters. In the second episode, he is indirectly mentioned by Cassie as "the other love of my life". Demoted to Extra:McKayis a fairly prominent character in the first season, but after he breaks it off with Cassie for good and brings an injured Nate to the hospital he is not seen for the rest of Season 2. Fiendish Fraternity: AfterMcKay's fraternity brothers see Cassie at a party, they pinMcKaydown and shout sexual things at him. He's deeply affected by the experience.

characters.name: BB Brookes
characters.description: A friend of the main group. Demoted to Extra: The first episode seems to set her up as being part of the main cast, or at least a prominent supporting character. After this, she largely falls to the wayside and mainly makes sporadic appearances. In Season 3, she makes a single appearance attending Cassie and Nate's wedding. Loose Lips: She's a heavy gossiper and can't keep a secret to save her life. When Kat tells her she lost her virginity, she knew it wouldn't be long before she told Maddy, Cassie "and the rest of the fucking planet Earth". Mama's Baby, Papa's Maybe: She's pregnant in Season 3. Given her personality, Maddy suspects she doesn't know who the father is. Must Have Nicotine: She is frequently seen vaping.

characters.name: Bishop
characters.description: The enigmatic, cool-headed and deadlyNumber Twoto Alamo. Bad People Abuse Animals: On Alamo's orders, he secretly kills Laurie's cockatoo pet Paladin by poisoning as a warning for messing with him. Beware the Quiet Ones: Bishop is calm and reserved, but he's the most dangerous of all Alamo's subordinates. He also betrays Alamo when he's thoroughly disgusted by the man. Bodyguard Betrayal: He doublecrosses Alamo at the very end, giving him an unloaded revolver to take Ali on. Though Alamo tries to cheat, he realizes too late and dies cursing Bishop. Even Evil Has Standards: He's a ruthless enforcer for Alamo, but it's implied his boss disgusts him with how he treats others and killed Rue. Bishop betrays Alamo to his death and then offers to give Maddy a ride home. He even allows Ali to depart in peace as he has no further quarrel with the man.

characters.name: Naz
characters.description: An Armenian mortician whom Nate borrowed money from. Upon learning that Nate spent a good chunk of that money on his wedding, he decides to make sure Nate pays him back, no matter what. Creepy Mortician: Puts people in coffins and decidesto do so with Nateto make sure he (actually Cassie) pays off his debt. Enemy Eats Your Lunch: When he has Cassie hostage, he enjoys coffee from her "#1 Hottie" mug. Evil Debt Collector: His role on the show is seeking his money back from Nate. He resorts toveryviolent and predatory means with full intent to torture and kill both Nate and Cassie. Eviler than Thou: He shows Nate that he's an amateur in lessons of brutality.

characters.name: Artur
characters.description: Naz's henchman. Whenever Nate has to be forced into being remembered to pay the money he owes to the former, this man is ordered to conduct the beatings. The Brute: He's big, not very bright, and handles violence for Naz. If Nate's being beaten up in Season 3, Artur is the one doing it. Given Name Reveal: Only named Artur inRain and Shine. Know When to Fold 'Em: When Alamo has a gun on him after shooting Naz, he gives Artur a chance to drop his gun. Realizing he has very little chance, Artur complies and proceeds to dig up Nate's coffin. Sinister Shades: Wears them in his second beating against Nate and when he abducted him at his construction site.

characters.name: Ellis
characters.description: Bondage Is Bad: He has a mummification kink and is very abusive and controlling towards Jules. The fact that he specifically likes wrapping Jules in plastic wrap like Dexter and casually says that he "slices women open for a living" just gives him serial killer vibes. Control Freak: He requires Jules to wear a long blond wig and becomes furious at Jules when he finds Rue's boxers on his bathroom floor. It appears that he doesn't like Jules interacting with others in general, as Jules, a free-spirited, adventurous, and outgoing person by nature, now lives like a hermit, rarely interacting with anyone besides Rue. On the few occasions she sees Rue and the others, she does so in secret. Hypocrite: Chews out Jules when he finds Rue's boxers while freaking out about STD's and his family finding out about his double life in the same breath. In the same scene, he talks about giving Jules a lot of freedom, when in reality, she's expected to cater to his desires in nearly every aspect of her life, down to the way she dresses, and she doesn't even have real privacy because she is expected to always be at his beck and call. Meal Ticket: He allows Jules to live in hisluxury DTLA penthouserent-free and funds her lavish lifestyle. Permission to Cheat: Jules claims that his wife knows about her relationship with Ellis. However, it's heavily implied that Ellis is lying, andSam Trammellexpressed doubts that Ellis's family even knows about his double life.

characters.name: Magick
characters.description: Bilingual Bonus: She speaks Spanish fluently, courtesy of Rosalía playing Magick. It's played for laughs when Rue gets in a shouting match with her, especially for those viewers who understand the language. Brutal Honesty: Magick has no problem being straightforward and blunt about Rue being up to no good working for Alamo. Jerkass Has a Point: Magick may be mean and nosy, but she's completely right to tell Big Eddy and Alamo that Rue should not be trusted after how she overheard her asking questions to Kitty over a group of guys having rough group sex with her. And in fact she is not, as Rue is actually working for the DEA to bring down his drug empire, though she didn't know that and had no way to prove it. But Rue planting the drugs she forgot to take out of Magick's locker, which was to discredit her initial accusation, further fuels and proves her suspicions about Rue right. Jerkass to One: Out of all Alamo's strippers, she is the meanest to Rue. No Sympathy: She feels little to no sadness over Tish's death, nor Angel's drug addiction, while claiming that she "ran away" from rehab.
